title: Whither Japan’s Three Non-Nuclear Principles?
gist: Tsuruoka Michito notes that Japan's three non-nuclear principles are being debated again as the Takaichi government prepares a new National Security Strategy due end-2026, with the realistic debate confined to the non-introduction principle while Japan remains in the NPT.

insights.claim: Debate over Japan's three non-nuclear principles has resurfaced as Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae's government prepares a new National Security Strategy due at the end of 2026.
insights.speaker: TSURUOKA Michito
insights.so_what: A shift in Japan's nuclear posture would be a major regional security and defense-spending signal.
insights.quote: Debate over the three non-nuclear principles has resurfaced in Japan as the government of Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae prepares a new National Security Strategy, due at the end of 2026.

insights.claim: The status of Japan's non-nuclear principles is itself contested: some see them as a foundational national principle (kokuze), others as a policy guideline the government can change.
insights.speaker: TSURUOKA Michito
insights.so_what: If treated as mere policy, revision faces lower political hurdles.

insights.claim: Japan's three non-nuclear principles—not possessing, producing, or permitting introduction of nuclear weapons—were announced by Prime Minister Sato Eisaku in 1967 and repeatedly reaffirmed by the Diet.
insights.speaker: TSURUOKA Michito
insights.so_what: Long institutional history raises the bar for change.
insights.locator: Prime Minister Sato Eisaku first announced

insights.claim: As long as Japan remains party to the NPT, the only practical debate is over the third principle of non-introduction, i.e., potentially allowing US nuclear weapons onto Japanese territory.
insights.speaker: TSURUOKA Michito
insights.so_what: Points to nuclear-sharing or port-call arrangements with the US as the realistic policy change to watch.
insights.quote: As long as Japan remains a party to the Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), the only practical debate concerns the third principle: non-introduction.
